lessons.title: Research and Fact-Checking with AI

cards.title: AI is a starting point
lines: Use AI to get an overview fast.
Then check with real sources.
Never stop at the AI's answer for important facts.

cards.title: Good first sources
lines: Manufacturer manuals and datasheets.
Standards from bodies such as IEC and IEEE. Many are paid.
Textbooks and university notes.
Official websites.

cards.title: Ask for sources, then open them
lines: Ask the AI to list its sources.
Open each one yourself.
Some listed sources may not exist.
If you cannot find it, do not use it.

cards.title: Check three things
lines: Is it from a trusted maker or body?
Is it recent? Firmware and standards change.
Do two independent sources agree?

cards.title: A second opinion
lines: It is like asking a second engineer to review your test sheet.
One source can be wrong.
Two independent sources agreeing is a better sign.

cards.title: Quick fact-check guide
lines: Match the claim to the right place to check.

cards.title: Example: does this relay have that function?
lines: The AI says a relay supports a function.
Open the datasheet and find the function list.
Write down the document name, version and date.

cards.title: When sources disagree
lines: For protection work, approved procedures and manufacturer documents win.
If the AI and the manual disagree, the manual wins.
If the manual is unclear, ask the manufacturer or a senior engineer.

cards.title: Practice: confirm one fact
lines: Ask an AI: What is IEC 61850, in simple words?
Find two trusted pages that confirm it.
Write their names and what matched.

cards.title: Recap
lines: Use AI for a quick overview.
Open the sources yourself.
Manuals and approved procedures settle disagreements.

quiz.q: What is the best way to use AI for research?
options: As a starting point, then verify
quiz.why: Use AI for an overview, then check real sources.

quiz.q: Where should a relay setting range be checked?
quiz.why: Manufacturer documents are the authority.

quiz.q: Why must you open the sources an AI lists?
options: Some may be invented or wrong
quiz.why: AI can invent sources.

quiz.q: If the AI and the manual disagree, which wins?
quiz.why: Manufacturer manuals and approved procedures win.

quiz.q: Which is a good sign that a fact is reliable?
quiz.why: Independent agreement from trusted sources is stronger.

lessons.career: Fast, careful research is one of the most useful AI-assisted skills for a service or testing engineer.

lessons.title: Reading Manuals and Datasheets with AI

cards.title: Manuals are long
lines: A relay manual can run to hundreds of pages.
You rarely need all of it.
AI can help you find the part you need.

cards.title: Datasheet or manual?
lines: Names vary by maker, but the roles are similar.

head: Document
What it is for
Example question
rows: Short summary of features and ratings
Details of each function and setting
How do I connect the supply?

cards.title: Use only documents you may use
lines: Public datasheets and manuals from the maker's website are usually fine to study.
Company-only or customer documents may not be allowed in public AI tools.
Check the rules before you upload anything.

cards.title: A guide, not the book
lines: AI is like a guide who helps you find the right chapter.
You still read the chapter yourself.

cards.title: Three safe ways to use AI with a manual
lines: Ask AI to explain a term. Then check the manual.
Ask AI for a reading plan: what to look up.
If your tool is approved for the document, ask it to find a section and give the page.

cards.title: Good questions
lines: Where in this document is the CT ratio explained?
List the protection functions named in this datasheet.
Explain 'time multiplier' in simple words.
What topics should I read before testing this function?

cards.title: Questions to avoid
lines: What setting should I use?
Is this safe to energise?
These need approved documents and a qualified engineer, not an AI guess.

cards.title: Example reading plan
lines: Ask: I will test an overcurrent function on a numerical relay. Make a reading plan for the manual.
A good plan lists topics such as: function description, setting ranges, wiring and inputs and outputs, test connection, tolerances, event records.
Then you open each topic in the manual.

cards.title: Ask for the page, then open it
lines: Ask for the section or page number.
Open it yourself.
If it is not there, do not use the answer.

cards.title: Practice: five terms
lines: Download a public datasheet for any relay model from the maker's website.
Pick 5 terms you do not know.
Ask an AI to explain each in simple words.
Check each one in the datasheet and note the page.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI helps you find and understand. The document is the authority.
Ask for page numbers and check them.
Use only documents you are allowed to use.

quiz.q: What is a good use of AI with a long manual?
options: Find which section to read and explain terms
quiz.why: AI is a guide to the document, not a replacement for it.

quiz.q: Which document is a short summary of features and ratings?
quiz.why: A datasheet summarises features and ratings.

quiz.q: Which question should you NOT rely on AI for?
options: Where is the CT ratio explained?
quiz.why: Settings come from approved documents and engineers.

quiz.q: An AI says 'see page 42'. What do you do?
quiz.why: Always open the page to confirm.

quiz.q: Which documents are usually fine to study with public AI tools?
options: Public manuals from the maker's website
quiz.why: Public documents are safer. Confidential ones need permission.

lessons.career: Finding the right page quickly saves hours when you test or service many relay models.

lessons.title: Summarising a Protection Relay Manual

cards.title: What a good summary has
lines: The purpose of the function.
The main settings in plain words.
Inputs and outputs.
What is usually tested.
Warnings.

cards.title: Summarise in small steps
lines: Do not paste the whole manual at once.
Take one chapter at a time.
Ask for a short summary, then ask follow-up questions.

cards.title: Prompt example (public document)
lines: Goal: Summarise this chapter about the overcurrent function in 10 bullet points.
Context: For a new technician. This is a public manual section.
Format: Bullets, then 5 terms with simple meanings.
Boundaries: Do not invent values. Write 'not stated' if the text does not say.

cards.title: Add a check step
lines: Ask the AI for the page or section behind each bullet.
Ask: What did you leave out?
Ask: Which parts are you unsure about?

cards.title: Check your summary
lines: Match each part of the summary to where you check it.

head: Summary item
How to check
rows: Open the table and read it

cards.title: Keep your own notes
lines: Rewrite the summary in your own words.
Write the page numbers.
Add 'ask a senior engineer' beside unclear parts.

cards.title: A summary is not the manual
lines: Never test from a summary alone.
Use the manufacturer's manual and your approved procedure on site.
Summaries can miss warnings.

cards.title: Privacy reminder
lines: Use public documents or approved tools.
Remove customer names and site details.

cards.title: Practice: summarise and check
lines: Take one public page about a relay function.
Ask an AI for a 10-bullet summary with page numbers.
Check three bullets against the page.
Write down anything that was wrong or missing.

cards.title: Recap
lines: Summarise one chapter at a time.
Ask for page numbers and check numbers and warnings yourself.
Never test from a summary.

quiz.q: How should you give a long manual to an AI?
quiz.why: Small parts give better, easier-to-check summaries.

quiz.q: Which part of a summary needs the closest check?
quiz.why: Numbers and units matter most and are easy to get wrong.

quiz.q: What should you write in the boundaries of your prompt?
options: Do not invent values; say 'not stated' if missing
quiz.why: This reduces made-up details.

quiz.q: Can you test a relay from an AI summary alone?
options: No, use the manual and approved procedure
quiz.why: Summaries can miss warnings and details.

quiz.q: Why ask 'What did you leave out?'
quiz.why: It exposes gaps you can then check in the manual.

lessons.career: Writing and checking your own summaries builds real understanding of each relay family you work on.

lessons.title: Checklists and Report Templates

cards.title: Why checklists help
lines: They stop you forgetting steps.
They make work the same every time.
AI can draft one quickly.

cards.title: What a test checklist usually covers
lines: These are common parts. Your company's procedure decides the real list.
Safety and permits.
Documents and settings received.
Visual checks.
Wiring and polarity checks.
Injection tests.
Contacts and indications.
Restoring and sign-off.

cards.title: Ask AI for a draft
lines: Goal: Make a pre-test checklist for a general overcurrent relay.
Context: For a new technician. Fictional training example.
Format: A table with Step, What to check, Result and Tick.
Boundaries: Do not give setting values. Write 'check approved procedure' where a limit is needed.

cards.title: A report layout (fictional)
lines: Use this as an idea for layout only.

head: Section
What goes in it
rows: As per the approved settings document
Test, expected (from approved criteria), measured, pass or fail

cards.title: Use fictional data only
lines: Use made-up names like Site A and Relay R1.
Use made-up numbers only to practise the layout.
Never present them as real results.

cards.title: Improve the template
lines: Ask for fewer fields.
Add a column for units.
Ask what is missing, then decide yourself.

cards.title: A template from AI is a draft
lines: Compare it with your company's format and approved procedures.
Only a qualified engineer signs a report.
Never publish a company template.

cards.title: Practice: one-page template
lines: Ask an AI for a one-page relay test report template using fictional data.
Check units, the pass or fail logic and the signature fields.
Edit it by hand and write what you changed.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI drafts. You check and edit.
Use fictional data for practice.
Approved procedures and company formats come first.

quiz.q: What is the main job of a checklist?
options: To stop missed steps and keep work consistent
quiz.why: Checklists make work consistent and complete.

quiz.q: What data should you use when practising templates?
quiz.why: Fictional data keeps real information safe.

quiz.q: What goes in the boundaries of the checklist prompt?
options: Do not give setting values; say 'check approved procedure'
quiz.why: Limits come from approved documents.

quiz.q: Who signs a real test report?
quiz.why: Engineers sign real reports.

quiz.q: Why add a units column?
options: It is a rule of Excel
quiz.why: Missing units cause mistakes.

lessons.career: Clear checklists and templates are the backbone of consistent testing and commissioning work.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting with AI Safely

cards.title: AI as a thinking partner
lines: It helps you list possible causes.
It does not see your equipment.
You decide what to check.

cards.title: Describe the problem clearly
lines: What did you do?
What did you expect?
What happened instead?
What have you already checked?

cards.title: Example (fictional)
lines: A trip output did not operate during a test on a training relay.
Expected: the contact closes.
Observed: no contact change.
Checked: the test set output is connected.
Ask: List possible causes, easiest to check first. Do not give settings.

cards.title: Easy checks first
lines: An AI might list ideas such as loose wiring, wrong terminals, a blocking signal, a disabled function or the wrong test setup.
Treat these as ideas only.
Confirm each one with the manual and drawings.

cards.title: Safety comes first
lines: Isolate and make safe before touching equipment.
Follow your permit and lock-out rules.
AI cannot tell if a circuit is live.
Never skip safe isolation because an AI said something.

cards.title: When to stop and ask
lines: If you are not sure, stop.
Ask a senior engineer.
Record what happened.

cards.title: Keep a log
lines: Write what you tried and what you saw.
Paste only non-confidential text to an AI.
A log helps the next person too.

cards.title: Good use and risky use
lines: Use the table as a quick guide.

head: Use
OK?
rows: Explain an error message in general
Decide if equipment is safe to energise
Change a setting because the AI said so

cards.title: Practice: a fictional fault
lines: Write a fictional fault in four lines: did, expected, happened, checked.
Ask an AI to list possible causes.
Mark each cause: check with manual, check with drawing, or ask a senior engineer.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI helps you think. You verify.
Safety and approved procedures come first.
If unsure, stop and ask.

quiz.q: What is AI's best role when troubleshooting?
quiz.why: AI can brainstorm. You verify and decide.

quiz.q: What should you do before touching equipment?
options: Isolate and make it safe following your rules
quiz.why: Safety rules and permits always come first.

quiz.q: Which is a good problem description?
options: What I did, expected, saw and already checked
quiz.why: Clear details give useful answers.

quiz.q: Can AI decide if a circuit is safe to energise?
quiz.why: AI cannot see or judge your equipment.

quiz.q: When you are unsure, you should...
options: Stop and ask a senior engineer
quiz.why: Stopping and asking is the safe choice.

resources.title: AI Fluency: Framework and Foundations (free, about 4 hours)

lessons.career: Calm, safe troubleshooting habits earn trust. AI can speed up thinking, but never replaces safe working.

lessons.title: Project: AI-Assisted Relay Test Checklist and Report Template

cards.title: Your project
lines: Make a one-page checklist and a one-page report template for testing a relay.
Use fictional data only.
Use AI to draft. You check and edit.

cards.title: What you will make
lines: A checklist (table).
A report template (one page).
A short note: what you changed and why.

cards.title: Step 1: Plan
lines: Write the goal and who it is for.
Pick one general function, for example overcurrent.
Decide the format: a table.

cards.title: Step 2: Draft with AI
lines: Use the four-part prompt: goal, context, format, boundaries.
Ask for the checklist first, then the report template.

cards.title: Step 3: Check against documents
lines: Compare with the testing section of a public manual or with training notes.
List steps that are missing or wrong.
Never trust the draft as it is.

cards.title: Step 4: Edit
lines: Add units, remove unclear steps and add a sign-off.
Keep a list of your changes.

cards.title: Step 5: Try it with fictional data
lines: Fill the template with made-up results for three tests.
Check that the pass or fail column makes sense.

cards.title: Educational only
lines: This is not an approved procedure.
Real tests follow your company's approved procedure and the manufacturer's documents.
Never publish a confidential template.

cards.title: How to judge your work
lines: Ask these four questions.

head: Check
Question
rows: Can a new technician follow it?
Does it include safety and sign-off?

cards.title: Practice: your portfolio note
lines: Write 3 lines: what you made, how AI helped, and how you checked it.
Example: I made a checklist and report template with fictional data. AI drafted both. I checked them against a public manual and edited them.

cards.title: Recap
lines: You used AI to draft documents, then checked and improved them.
Fictional data and approved procedures kept it safe.
Keep your note for your portfolio.

quiz.q: Who is responsible for the final checklist?
quiz.why: AI drafts. You check and own the result.

quiz.q: What data does this project use?
quiz.why: Only fictional data is used.

quiz.q: Which step compares the draft with real documents?
quiz.why: Checking against documents finds missing or wrong steps.

quiz.q: Is this checklist an approved procedure?
options: Yes if the AI wrote it
quiz.why: Real work uses approved procedures.

quiz.q: What goes in your portfolio note?
options: What you made, how AI helped, how you checked
quiz.why: A short honest note shows your process.

lessons.career: This small project shows an employer that you can use AI to draft documents safely and check them like an engineer.
